detail: The statutes this room is built from: Magna Carta's clause 35 (one measure, one weight, without defining units); the 1688 survey finding the Exchequer no longer held the wine-gallon standard; 1695 Ireland lodging standards in the Exchequer and sending copies to counties; 1706 Scotland requiring every burgh to keep duplicates; the 1495 Winchester definitions measuring capacity 'by stricken' (level, not heaped); the 1835 Act making heaped measure illegal; alnage — cloth ordered uniform from 1196, enforced by an alnager who measured each piece and affixed a stamp, faulty cloth forfeit to the Crown; the 1353 repeal of the single width rule.
note: The customs house borrows the history of standards and measures, not the text. Single sizes break when goods diversify, so the fare is bands rather than a boolean.
